Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK/function-calling next steps

Hi Tara —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and to capture next steps: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Current pain: long-tail hallucinations in customer support summarization and high token cost for high-volume queries.
- Goal: reduce per-request token cost while maintaining or improving summary fidelity; enable deterministic structured outputs for downstream ingestion (ticketing + analytics).

Product / integration fit (notes from the call)
- SDK changes: you’ll likely want the sandbox SDK flows; lightweight client-side call with server-side function-calling fallback for private data lookups. We discussed our JS and Python SDKs; engineering prefers Python for batch/RPC jobs.
- Function calling: recommended pattern is function-call for lookups (customer profile, ticket metadata) to avoid exposing PII to the model and to produce structured JSON outputs.
- Streaming: use streaming for the UI summaries to improve perceived latency; batch/stream hybrid covers both throughput and UX.
- Structured outputs: we can enforce schema via function-calling + Redwood structured-output validators to reduce post-processing.
- Embeddings & reranking: suggested flow is embeddings for semantic search + a light reranker for top-K precision on support suggestions. Quantized model variants for embeddings can keep costs low.

Open technical asks from your team
- Expected median latency SLO for interactive summary endpoints (you mentioned ~300ms target).
- Typical sequence length distribution for your support use-case (avg and 95th percentile).
- Any regulatory constraints on embeddings storage or KMS requirements.

Next steps
- I’ll share a mutual action plan (attached) with an initial technical deep-dive scheduled.
- Rishi (cc’d) will follow up on quantization/latency profiles and sizing.
- Proposed date for technical deep-dive: Thu May 14, 11am PT — let me know if that works.

Attachments: redwood-integration-brief.pdf, mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,

Marissa / Tara / Daniel —

Quick technical notes (high level) to feed the agenda: 

1) Model + quantization recommendation
- For mixed workload (interactive 400 token avg, 3k tail) we recommend a 16-bit FP model variant for the tail and 8-bit quantized variant for median interactive traffic. On Dedicated you can run a split routing policy: serve P0 interactive requests on the 8-bit quantized variant with prefix caching, and route large-context requests to the 16-bit variant. This keeps P95 low while preserving long-context fidelity.

2) Latency estimates (approx)
- Hosted (managed): 450–550ms P95 for 3k context on quantized variants; 220–320ms P95 for 400 token interactive on optimized quantized runtime with batching turned off for low-latency routes.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity, GPU-optimized): 280–360ms P95 for 400 tokens (config-dependent), 420–600ms P95 for 3k context.

3) Streaming + batch hybrid
- Suggest streaming for UI summaries to improve perceived latency; combine with micro-batching for background rerank/embeddings pipelines to reduce cost. We’ll propose a hybrid in the sample config.

4) Embeddings encryption / KMS
- We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) for embeddings at-rest encryption in Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys for enterprise plans. Retention policy can be configured per-account; recommend 90–365 days depending on compliance.

I’ll pull example SLO numbers and a cost delta table for quantization variants to share in the deep-dive.

—Rishi
